He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Eastern Kentucky Colonels men's basketball|Eastern Kentucky Colonels]] and the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]]. ==High school career== Green played basketball for [[Detroit Country Day School]] in [[Beverly Hills, Michigan]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 19.5 points, eight assists and seven rebounds per game.{{cite web |last=Goricki |first=David |title=Detroit Country Day star Wendell Green leaving for La Lumiere |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/2018/08/09/wendell-green-leaving-detroit-country-day-indiana-prep-school-la-lumiere/952978002/ |website=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=November 14, 2021 |date=August 9, 2018}} For his junior season, Green transferred to [[La Lumiere School]] in [[La Porte, Indiana]].{{cite web |last=Farrell |first=Perry A. |title=Detroit Country Day star Wendell Green Jr. transferring to La Lumiere |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/08/09/wendell-green-jr-la-lumiere-detroit-country-day/949061002/ |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |access-date=November 14, 2021 |date=August 9, 2018}} At La Lumiere, he played alongside teammates [[Isaiah Stewart]], [[Keion Brooks Jr.]], [[Jaden Ivey]], [[Jeremy Sochan]] and [[Kamari Lands]]. As a junior, he helped his team reach the title game at [[GEICO]] Nationals.{{cite web |last=Durando |first=Bennett |title=Wendell Green Jr. takes torch as Auburn basketball's next audacious point guard |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/auburn/2021/11/08/wendell-green-jr-auburn-basketballs-next-fearless-point-guard/6292015001/ |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |access-date=November 14, 2021 |date=November 8, 2021}} Green committed to playing college basketball for [[Eastern Kentucky Colonels men's basketball|Eastern Kentucky]] over offers from [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]], [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]] and [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]].{{cite web |last=Skol |first=Mark Jr. |date=June 25, 2020 |title=Basketball star Wendell Green Jr. grew in two seasons at La Lumiere |url=https://www.wndu.com/content/sports/Basketball-star-Wendell-Green-Jr-grew-in-two-seasons-at-La-Lumiere-571491001.html |access-date=November 14, 2021 |website=[[WNDU-TV]]}} ==College career== On January 2, 2021, Green posted a freshman season-high 30 points and five rebounds for Eastern Kentucky in an 80–75 win against [[Austin Peay Governors basketball|Austin Peay]].{{cite web |title=Green Jr.'s 30-Point Performance Leads Men's Basketball to Road Win at Austin Peay |url=https://ekusports.com/news/2021/1/2/green-jrs-30-point-performance-leads-mens-basketball-to-road-win-at-austin-peay.aspx |website=Eastern Kentucky University Athletics |access-date=November 14, 2021 |date=January 2, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 15.8 points, five assists, 3.4 rebounds and 1.6 steals per game, earning First Team All-[[Ohio Valley Conference]] (OVC) and All-Newcomer Team honors. He was a five-time OVC Freshman of the Week selection.{{cite web |last=Clemente |first=Christian |title=Wendell Green Jr. arrives at Auburn with 'a chip on his shoulder' |url=https://auburn.rivals.com/news/wendell-green-jr-arrives-at-auburn-with-a-chip-on-his-shoulder- |website=AuburnSports |access-date=November 14, 2021 |date=May 30, 2021}} For his sophomore season, Green transferred to [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]].{{cite web |last=Green |first=Tom |title=EKU transfer Wendell Green Jr. seems like ideal fit for Auburn basketball at point guard |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2021/04/eku-transfer-wendell-green-jr-seems-like-ideal-fit-for-auburn-basketball-at-point-guard.html |website=AL.com |access-date=November 14, 2021 |date=April 10, 2021}} Green would earn 2nd team All-SEC honors during his junior year. Green would break the Auburn record for most consecutive free throw makes without a miss, hitting 28 straight free throws. Two seasons later, Green’s record was broken by Chad Baker-Mazara. Following his junior season, Green elected to forgo the remainder of his college eligibility and enter the [[2023 NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Green joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |date=June 29, 2023 |title=Cavaliers Announce 2023 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-summer-league-roster-230629 |access-date=June 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On October 28, 2023, Green was selected in the 2023 NBA G League draft by the [[Maine Celtics]],{{cite web|title=Maine Celtics Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/training-camp-roster-102823|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=October 28, 2023}} but was waived on November 9.{{cite web|title=Maine Celtics Finalize Roster|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/roster-set-110923|website=NBA.com|date=November 9, 2023|access-date=December 13, 2023}} In January 2024, Green signed with [[OKK Novi Pazar]].{{cite news |last=Obradovic |first=Igor |date=15 January 2024 |title=Wendell Green Jr. agreed terms with Novi Pazar |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Serbia/news/847972/Wendell-Green-Jr.-agreed-terms-with-Novi-Pazar |access-date=25 July 2024 |work=[[Eurobasket.com]]}} In 14 league games, he averaged 20.8 points and 4.3 assists per game. In July, he played for the War Ready in [[The Basketball Tournament]]. Following the tournament, he joined [[Indios de San Francisco de Macorís]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]]. On 25 July 2024, Green signed with Keflavík of the Icelandic [[Úrvalsdeild karla (basketball)|Úrvalsdeild karla]] for the [[2024–25 Úrvalsdeild karla (basketball)|2024–2025 season]].{{cite news |date=25 July 2024 |title=Wendell Green Jr. semur við Keflavík |url=https://www.facebook.com/keflavikkarfa/posts/pfbid0jZywgjsESDisqM4eaMvncoMNAfEjzxnKBVGgiLMgodSzT2n6dZQTcaJDwSTkjSAol |access-date=25 July 2024 |work=[[Keflavík men's basketball]] |language=is |via=[[Facebook]]}} On 28 September, he won the [[Icelandic Men's Basketball Supercup|Icelandic Super Cup]] after Keflavík defeated reigning national champions [[Valur men's basketball|Valur]] 98–88 in the cup final.{{cite news |author=Stefán Marteinn Ólafsson |date=28 September 2024 |title=Uppgjörið: Keflavík - Þór Ak. 82-86 - Þór skellti meisturunum |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20242627182d/uppgjorid-keflavik-thor-ak.-82-86-thor-skellti-meisturunum |access-date=28 September 2024 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |language=is}} He was released by Keflavík in November after averaging 23.2 points on 37% shooting in five Úrvalsdeild games.{{cite news |author=Óskar Ófeigur Jónsson |date=5 November 2024 |title=Fjórði stigahæsti kaninn en sá með lélegustu skotnýtinguna |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20242645285d/fjordi-stigahaesti-kaninn-en-sa-med-lelegustu-skotnytinguna |access-date=6 November 2024 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |language=is}} On 30
